relevance_note: Case report of a man and his infant son with PAPA syndrome: "the patient as well as his son were both heterozygous for a pathogenic missense E250K mutation in the PSTPIP1 gene", plus a literature table of five earlier E250K patients.
method_note: Rows built with a short Python script from my own reading; all spans checked verbatim against the paper by script. In scope: the index patient (43-year-old man, label 'patient'), his infant son ('son of patient'; inheritance recorded as inherited paternal because the paper states the father carries the same variant), the five literature patients of Table I (no label column, so 'Table I row 1'-'Table I row 5', with the Author (y) cell as source_reference_in_review), and one previously reported E250K patient with FSGS cited in the Discussion ('ref 10 patient'; may or may not overlap a Table I patient, the paper does not say). Table I patients: variant E250K taken from the table caption, which names the group ('patients with E250K mutations'); the caption misprints the gene as 'PTSPIP1', so the gene symbol was taken from the text sentence ('E250K mutation of the PSTPIP1 gene ... (Table I)'). The Table I 'Age (y)' column does not say whether it is age at report, diagnosis or onset; recorded as age at last evaluation. 'Effective treatment(s)' column copied into treatment_summary. Table I 'osteomyelitis' (row 3) was not mapped to the checklist item 'sterile osteomyelitis' because sterility is not stated. Hepatosplenomegaly (row 3) was mapped to both splenomegaly and hepatomegaly. Index patient: the variant is printed as 'E250K' and 'c.748 glycine to adenine in exon 11' (non-HGVS cDNA wording); both recorded as printed, no transcript printed. 'Absence of other PAMI features such as hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and growth failure' was recorded as excluded rows for those terms only; under the narrow/broad rule it does not exclude splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia or the composite 'growth failure or failure to thrive' checklist item. Negative HSV/VZV PCR, stains and tissue cultures recorded as excluded findings by D-27. Age at diagnosis given only as 'adulthood'. Sepsis is a single episode, so 'recurrent infections' left not reported. Not attributed to anyone: 'Additional features present in other cases with the E250K mutation include splenomegaly, bleeding diathesis, and serious cutaneous and pulmonary infections.^6' (plural, not person-specific); 'Renal disease has not been reported in previous cases of E250K PAPA syndrome' (a statement about reporting, not a named-group absence). Contradictions/inconsistencies: the text says '6 previously reported patients with the E250K mutation' and calls this 'the seventh published case', but Table I lists only five patients. n_patients_reported and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the paper states neither.

first_author.span: Authors: Zhao Raymond; Novice Taylor; Konda Sasank

individual_label_in_paper.span: A 43-year-old man with a history of kidney transplantation

is_proband.span: We present the seventh published case of PAPA syndrome secondary to the E250K mutation.

age_at_diagnosis_original_text.span: our patient was not formally diagnosed until adulthood

treatment_summary.value: Transplant immunosuppression with mycophenolate mofetil and tacrolimus; earlier chronic cyclosporine for PG; empiric vancomycin then linezolid, acyclovir and prednisone with minimal improvement; canakinumab (interleukin-1 beta inhibitor) with near complete resolution of acneiform lesions and significant improvement in arthritis
span: The patient’s transplant immunosuppressive regimen consisted of mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily and tacrolimus 1.5 mg daily.
He was treated empirically with vancomycin followed by linezolid, acyclovir, and prednisone with minimal improvement observed.
Canakinumab, an interleukin-1β inhibitor, was initiated with near complete resolution of the patient’s acneiform lesions and significant improvement in his arthritis.
After 3 months of canakinumab, there is near resolution of all prior lesions without scarring.

disease_label_as_stated.span: Both father and son were formally diagnosed with PAPA syndrome.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Genetic testing (heterozygous PSTPIP1 E250K) together with the clinical picture; PAPA favoured over PAMI because of the classic clinical triad and absence of other PAMI features
span: Genetic testing confirmed that the patient as well as his son were both heterozygous for a pathogenic missense E250K mutation in the PSTPIP1 gene
PAPA syndrome was deemed more likely given his classic clinical triad as well as the absence of other PAMI features such as hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and growth failure
